ver_001: You can recognise it by its tall crown rising beside the Roman Arena, its roots recently anchored with concrete piles after a 2025 scare. It stands in Piazza Bra, among the square's circular flowerbeds.
ver_002: You can recognise it by its huge trunk, over five metres round, filling most of the small garden. It stands at the centre of Piazza Indipendenza, beside a ginkgo.
ver_003: You can recognise it as the group of ginkgos sharing the small garden with the square's much taller plane tree. It stands in Piazza Indipendenza.
ver_004: You can recognise it by its tall crown rising over the avenue, reaching 28 metres. It stands on Viale Nino Bixio, in Borgo Trento, between the city hospital and Ponte Garibaldi.
ver_005: You can recognise it as the avenue of cypresses climbing from the palace toward the grotto, mixing younger replanted trees with older survivors. It stands along the main axis of Giardino Giusti.
